expectation: hasEnded compares minutesBetween(at, endAt), whole minutes truncated toward zero, with 0, so a closure with less than one minute left (for example 30 seconds) counts as ended: adding it is rejected and it is left out of the upcoming closures.
finding: - `src/schedules/closures.mjs:26` with `src/schedules/front-desk-service.mjs:31,56` (governing rules: Time limits and expiry, "A desk closure ... whose `endAt` is not later than `now()` is rejected"; "Upcoming desk closures are the building's active closures whose `endAt` is later than `now()`"): `hasEnded` truncates the remaining time to whole minutes with `minutesBetween(at, closure.endAt) <= 0`, so a closure that is still open but ends in less than one minute is treated as ended. Concrete case: `endAt = now() + 30000` makes `minutesBetween` return 0, so `addClosure` rejects a closure that the spec accepts, and `upcomingClosures` omits an active closure whose `endAt` is later than `now()`. Fix: compare the instants directly, `closure.endAt <= at`.

expectation: The single withdraw rule for waiting and offered entries carries the 60-minute cutoff, so a waiting entry whose startAt is less than 60 minutes from now cannot be withdrawn, although the limit applies only to offered entries.
finding: - `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:58-64`, `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:7,19-26`, `src/waitlist/queue.mjs:9-13` (governing rules: Waitlist, "Only a nonexpired `offered` entry may be accepted"; Time limits, "A waitlist offer is expired when `now()` is equal to or later than its `expiresAt`"): An expired offer can be accepted. `acceptOffer` calls `moveEntry(entry, 'accept', at)`, which sets `state` to `accepted` before the guard `isLapsing(next, at)` runs (line 61). `isLapsing` requires `state === 'offered'`, so on the already-accepted copy it is always false, and the expired check never fires. Failure case: an entry with `state: 'offered'` and `expiresAt` equal to or earlier than `now()` is saved as `accepted`. Fix: check the input before the transition, e.g. `if (isExpired(entry, at)) throw new Error('offer has expired');`, or reject when `!isLiveOffer(entry, at)`.

expectation: The single withdraw rule for waiting and offered entries carries the 60-minute cutoff, so a waiting entry whose startAt is less than 60 minutes from now cannot be withdrawn, although the limit applies only to offered entries.
finding: - `src/waitlist/entry-states.mjs:9,22`, `src/waitlist/waitlist-service.mjs:66-71` (governing rule: Time limits, "Withdrawing an `offered` waitlist entry is rejected when its `startAt` is less than 60 minutes after `now()`. A `waiting` entry has no such limit."): Withdrawal of a `waiting` entry is blocked inside the 60-minute window. The `withdraw` rule at line 9 lists `['waiting', 'offered']` together and attaches `cutoff: WITHDRAW_CUTOFF_MINUTES`, and line 22 then rejects any entry with `entry.startAt - at < minutes(60)`. A `waiting` entry starting in 30 minutes is therefore rejected, though the spec places no limit on it. Fix: apply the cutoff only to the `offered` source, e.g. split the rule into `from: ['waiting']` without cutoff and `from: ['offered']` with cutoff.

expectation: ENTRY_DEFAULTS gives active: true and prepareRoom spreads it under the room entry, so a room entry without an active value becomes active and is selected for the report, although only rooms whose active value is true may be.
finding: - `src/utilization/room-directory.mjs:7,10,36` (governing rule: Utilization reports, "only rooms whose `active` value is `true` ... are selected"; Rooms, "Only rooms whose `active` value is `true` may be booked or listed"): A room entry without an `active` field is treated as active. `ENTRY_DEFAULTS` sets `active: true`, and the filter at line 36 then admits it. Under the governing rule a missing `active` value is not `true`, so such a room must be excluded from the report. The reservation catalog applies the strict check `room.active === true` (`src/reservations/catalog.mjs:12`), so the two modules disagree. Fix: remove the `active: true` default, or default it to `false`, so only an explicit `true` selects a room.

expectation: A credit reason is trimmed instead of being stored exactly as supplied.
finding: - `src/billing/invoice-request.mjs:12` (governing rule: Invoices, "its `reason` must not be blank after trimming; the reason is stored exactly as supplied"): The credit reason is stored trimmed. `prepareCredit` checks `trimmed(credit.reason)` correctly but then returns `reason: credit.reason.trim()`, so a supplied reason of `"  promo  "` is stored as `"promo"` and the stored credit and the invoice `credits` no longer match the request. Fix: return `reason: credit.reason`.

expectation: paymentStatus passes the invoice record current to netPaid as its invoiceId argument; netPaid compares each intent's invoiceId (a string) with it using ===, and a string never equals an object, so no intent matches and the status reports paid 0 even after an intent of the invoice was captured.
finding: - `src/payments/payment-service.mjs:54`, `src/payments/payment-policy.mjs:53-55` (governing rule: Time limits and expiry, "A payment status reports `dueAt`, `late` and `paid`, the sum of `captured` minus `refunded` over its `captured` and `refunded` intents"): The payment status always reports `paid` as 0 for an invoice that has payments. `netPaid(intents, invoiceId)` compares `intent.invoiceId === invoiceId`, but `paymentStatus` passes the whole `current` invoice object (`netPaid(await store.list(), current)`), so no intent ever matches. Failure case: an invoice with one captured intent of 1000 and no refunds yields `paid: 0` instead of 1000. Fix: pass the id, i.e. `netPaid(await store.list(), current.id)`.

expectation: releaseTime rounds now() up to a whole minute with minuteStart(at + MINUTE - 1) and then adds wait, but wait is counted from the local minute of day, which localMinuteOfDay takes from the start of the current minute; when now() is not on a minute boundary the result is one minute late (22:59:30 local with endMinute 23:00 gives 23:01 instead of 23:00), so releaseAt is not the first minute boundary after now() whose local minute is endMinute.
finding: - `src/messaging/quiet-hours.mjs:32-36` (governing rule: Message delivery, "`releaseAt` at the first minute boundary after `now()` whose local minute is `endMinute`"): The release time is off by one minute. `minuteStart(at + MINUTE - 1)` gives the next boundary, whose local minute is `minute + 1`, but `wait` is computed from the local minute of `at` (`minute`), not of that boundary. Concrete case: `at = 30000` ms (epoch plus 30 s), offset 0, `endMinute = 5`. The first boundary after `now()` with local minute 5 is `300000`; the code computes `wait = 5`, giving `60000 + 5 * 60000 = 360000`, i.e. 00:06 instead of 00:05. Fix: compute `wait` from the local minute of the boundary, e.g. `const boundary = minuteStart(at + MINUTE - 1); const wait = (endMinute - localMinuteOfDay(boundary, offset) + DAY_MINUTES) % DAY_MINUTES;` and return `boundary + minutes(wait)`.

expectation: formatList writes each item through formatText, so a list item that starts with =, +, - or @ gets the ' prefix (for example the list ['-a', 'b'] is written '-a;b), although only text values get that prefix and a list's items are written as stored.
finding: - `src/exports/value-format.mjs:27-30` (governing rule: CSV exports, "a `list` of strings is joined with `;`, its items written as stored"): List items are passed through `formatText`, which prefixes a `'` to any item starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. A room amenity such as `-quiet` is therefore exported as `'-quiet` instead of as stored. Fix: join the list items as stored, e.g. `value.join(';')` after the type check, and keep the formula prefix only in the `text` formatter.

expectation: hasAmenities compares the size of the union with room.amenities.length; after lowercasing, a room amenity list with duplicates (Whiteboard, whiteboard) has a union smaller than its length, so that room is never eligible even when it has every requested amenity.
finding: - `src/reservations/catalog.mjs:16`: Governing rule (Rooms): "a room must contain every requested amenity." `hasAmenities` compares the size of the union of room and requested amenities with `room.amenities.length`. If a room's stored amenity list contains a duplicate, e.g. `['wifi','wifi']`, a request for `['wifi']` yields a union size of 1 against a length of 2 and is wrongly rejected as unavailable, even though the room contains the amenity. Fix: test containment directly, e.g. `amenities.every((amenity) => room.amenities.includes(amenity))`.

expectation: applyTransition copies the record with a shallow spread and then pushes onto next.history, which is the same array as the received record's history, so confirm, cancel and reschedule modify the reservation object they receive.
finding: - `src/reservations/transitions.mjs:17`, `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:53-67`: Governing rule (Conventions): "Operations never modify a reservation object they receive; they return new records." `applyTransition` makes a shallow copy with `{...record}` and then calls `next.history.push(...)`, which mutates the `history` array shared with the input record. Canceling or rescheduling therefore appends an entry to the caller's original reservation object. Fix: copy the array, e.g. `next.history = [...record.history, {state: rule.to, at}]`.

expectation: rescheduleReservation never applies the 240-minute duration limit to the snapped new window.
finding: - `src/reservations/reservation-service.mjs:53-68`, `src/reservations/policy.mjs:1-3` (governing rule: Rescheduling, "the snapped window must satisfy the duration limit and be available"): Rescheduling does not enforce the 240-minute duration limit. `rescheduleReservation` snaps the new window and checks only availability and `endAt > startAt`; `exceedsMaxDuration` is called only in `createReservation` (line 14). A reschedule to a window longer than 240 minutes is accepted and stored. Fix: call `exceedsMaxDuration(window)` in `rescheduleReservation` before the availability check and reject with the same duration error.

expectation: recordBadgeEvent looks up the event key through findKeyedEvent(store, prepared), which reads store.list(event); the event carries the event's buildingId, which the badge store (createAppendLog) destructures as a building filter, so a key already recorded for an event in another building is not found and the event is recorded again.
finding: - `src/badges/badge-service.mjs:5-7,15-17`, `src/platform/append-log.mjs:6-8` (governing rule: Request keys, "A badge event's `eventKey` ... if an event recorded in any building has the key, recording returns it and does no further work"): The event-key duplicate check is limited to the submitted building. `findKeyedEvent` calls `store.list(event)`, and the store's `list` filters by `buildingId` when it is supplied, so an event with the same `eventKey` recorded in a different building is not found and a duplicate is recorded. Fix: search all recorded events for the key (for example, call `store.list()` with no building filter and match `eventKey`), while keeping the repeated-swipe and anomaly checks building-scoped.

expectation: countedReservations tests overlaps(instant(startAt), period), but instant is a zero-length interval and overlaps uses strict comparisons, so a confirmed reservation starting exactly at the first instant of the month is not counted in used minutes, although the month is half-open and its start is inside it.
finding: - `src/members/allowance.mjs:9-13,22` (governing rule: Selection and counting, "A member's used minutes are the total length in minutes of the member's `confirmed` reservations whose `startAt` is within the month"; Member directory, "the month" being the half-open UTC month from `usageMonth`): Reservations that start exactly at the first instant of the month are not counted. `countedReservations` tests `overlaps(instant(reservation.startAt), period)`, and the zero-length `instant` fails the strict test `right.startAt < left.endAt` when `left.startAt === period.startAt`. Failure case: a confirmed 60-minute reservation starting at `Date.UTC(year, month - 1, 1)` is left out of `used`, `remaining` and `reservationIds`. Fix: test the half-open containment directly, e.g. `period.startAt <= reservation.startAt && reservation.startAt < period.endAt`.

expectation: summarizeActors counts the entries returned by selectEntries, which keeps only the first limit matches, so an actor summary stops counting at the query limit (500 when absent), although an actor summary counts every entry its (valid) query matches, ignoring limit.
finding: - `src/audit/audit-query.mjs:41,49-51`, `src/platform/listing.mjs:1` (governing rule: Selection and counting, "An actor summary ... counts every entry it matches, ignoring `limit`"): The actor summary is truncated by the query limit. `summarizeActors` iterates `selectEntries(...)`, and `selectEntries` calls `pageOf(...)`, which returns `.slice(0, page.limit)`. An actor summary query with `limit: 2` over five matching entries therefore counts only the first two, so the reported `entries` values are understated. Fix: count from the filtered, unsliced matches (for example, `entries.filter((entry) => matches(entry, query, at))`) and leave `limit` to the query listing only.

expectation: quoteField doubles inner double quotes with /"/ without the g flag, so replace doubles only the first one and a field with two or more double quotes is written as malformed CSV (the field a"b"c is written as "a""b"c" instead of "a""b""c").
finding: - `src/exports/csv-format.mjs:7` (governing rule: CSV exports, "A field containing a comma, double quote, carriage return or line feed is wrapped in double quotes, with inner double quotes doubled"): Only the first inner double quote is doubled. `text.replace(/"/, '""')` has no `g` flag, so a value such as `say "hi" now` is written as `"say ""hi" now"`, which is not a valid quoted CSV field. expectation: sendMessage starts store.save without awaiting it and then awaits send; the outbox store applies each write later through its write queue, so send receives the message before the queued write of the sent message completes.
finding: - `src/messaging/messaging-service.mjs:53-56` (governing rule: Message delivery, "A message created outside quiet hours is saved as `sent` with `sentAt` from `now()` before `send` receives `{messageId, memberId, body}`"; Saving before notifying): The message is sent before it is saved. `store.save(sent)` is called without `await` and its promise is stored in `saved`; `send(...)` then runs while the write is still only queued in the store's `writes` chain. A failed or delayed save can therefore be preceded by a delivered notice. Fix: `const saved = await store.save(sent);` before `await send(sentNotice(sent));`.

releaseTime rounds now() up to a whole minute with minuteStart(at + MINUTE - 1) and then adds wait, but wait is counted from the local minute of day, which localMinuteOfDay takes from the start of the current minute; when now() is not on a minute boundary the result is one minute late (22:59:30 local with endMinute 23:00 gives 23:01 instead of 23:00), so releaseAt is not the first minute boundary after now() whose local minute is endMinute.

formatList writes each item through formatText, so a list item that starts with =, +, - or @ gets the ' prefix (for example the list ['-a', 'b'] is written '-a;b), although only text values get that prefix and a list's items are written as stored.

acceptOffer checks expiry with isLapsing(next, at), where next is the record returned by the accept transition, whose state is already accepted, while isLapsing is true only for an offered entry; so the check never fires and an expired offer can be accepted.

finding: - `src/exports/csv-format.mjs:7` (governing rule: CSV exports, "A field containing a comma, double quote, carriage return or line feed is wrapped in double quotes, with inner double quotes doubled"): Only the first inner double quote is doubled. `text.replace(/"/, '""')` has no `g` flag, so a value such as `say "hi" now` is written as `"say ""hi" now"`, which is not a valid quoted CSV field. This affects every `text` and `list` column written through `formatLine`. Fix: use `text.replace(/"/g, '""')`.

applyTransition copies the record with a shallow spread and then pushes onto next.history, which is the same array as the received record's history, so confirm, cancel and reschedule modify the reservation object they receive.
rescheduleReservation never applies the 240-minute duration limit to the snapped new window.

recordBadgeEvent looks up the event key through findKeyedEvent(store, prepared), which reads store.list(event); the event carries the event's buildingId, which the badge store (createAppendLog) destructures as a building filter, so a key already recorded for an event in another building is not found and the event is recorded again.

countedReservations tests overlaps(instant(startAt), period), but instant is a zero-length interval and overlaps uses strict comparisons, so a confirmed reservation starting exactly at the first instant of the month is not counted in used minutes, although the month is half-open and its start is inside it.

summarizeActors counts the entries returned by selectEntries, which keeps only the first limit matches, so an actor summary stops counting at the query limit (500 when absent), although an actor summary counts every entry its (valid) query matches, ignoring limit.

quoteField doubles inner double quotes with /"/ without the g flag, so replace doubles only the first one and a field with two or more double quotes is written as malformed CSV (the field a"b"c is written as "a""b"c" instead of "a""b""c").

sendMessage starts store.save without awaiting it and then awaits send; the outbox store applies each write later through its write queue, so send receives the message before the queued write of the sent message completes.

replan(ticket, null) deletes plannedWork from its copy, but clearPlannedWork spreads the original ticket first and that copy second; spreading only overrides keys that exist, so the saved ticket keeps its old plannedWork: it is still listed as the room's planned work, still blocks other tickets' windows, and the ticket can never be planned again because planWork rejects a ticket that already has a planned window.

intentRequest rebuilds the request from a fixed list of invoice fields that leaves out issuedAt, so newIntent, which computes the fee with lateFee(prepared.total, prepared.issuedAt, at), gets a due instant of NaN and an intent created while its invoice is late has a fee of 0 and an amount equal to the total.

hasEnded compares minutesBetween(at, endAt), whole minutes truncated toward zero, with 0, so a closure with less than one minute left (for example 30 seconds) counts as ended: adding it is rejected and it is left out of the upcoming closures.

The single withdraw rule for waiting and offered entries carries the 60-minute cutoff, so a waiting entry whose startAt is less than 60 minutes from now cannot be withdrawn, although the limit applies only to offered entries.

ENTRY_DEFAULTS gives active: true and prepareRoom spreads it under the room entry, so a room entry without an active value becomes active and is selected for the report, although only rooms whose active value is true may be.
A credit reason is trimmed instead of being stored exactly as supplied.
